reasoning: Combined the overlapping fill-in guidance into one edit, preserving the distinction between asking for an entity's full canonical name and explicitly requesting only a missing name component. Retained the unique guidance on integral title words, unsupported subtypes, and definition categories. The other edits independently clarify exact answer wording and distinguish source works or people from adaptations and parodies.

edits.target: For fill-in or clue-style prompts, supply only the missing headword or name component; do not repeat information already given in the clue or add clue modifiers unless they are part of the canonical answer.
edits.content: For fill-in or clue-style prompts, give the full conventional answer at the requested level of specificity, without explanation. If the clue asks for an entity identified by an established multiword proper name, title, or label, return its full canonical form, retaining words integral to the name (such as a publication-type word) even if part appears in the clue. If the prompt explicitly asks to complete a supplied name or requests only the missing component, give only that component. Otherwise, do not repeat clue text or add modifiers. Do not add an unsupported subtype or narrow a generic category merely because context mentions one; for definition clues, give the category that directly matches the definition, not a related role or narrower example.

edits.target: - Treat equivalent paraphrases as matches, prefer direct statements or definitions over tangential references, and ignore irrelevant distractors.
edits.content: - Prefer the exact term and grammatical form used by the strongest direct statement, especially when echoed by the question, over synonymous or broader wording. Use paraphrases as evidence for equivalence, not as interchangeable final-answer wording; ignore tangential references and irrelevant distractors.

edits.target: When a question describes a title as changed, adapted, or parodied, distinguish the original title from the altered title. Use the wording to determine which is requested: a reference to the original work or an author's title asks for the original; a question asking what the adaptation, parody, or short was called asks for the altered title. Do not mistake the described change for the requested answer.
edits.content: When a clue concerns an adaptation, retelling, or parody, determine whether it asks for the source work or original character, or for the new work or title. If it asks what an adaptation or parody was called, give that altered title; if it asks what work or person it draws on or parodies, give the source work or original person—not the adaptation or the tale that features the parody. Use the clue's wording to identify the requested relation.
